claims.text: Using an MTP trained on TaVCrW DFT data with FEP will reduce computational cost by more than 80% relative to EAM-based TOR-TILD.
The MTP+FEP workflow will achieve a free-energy error below 0.5 meV/atom.
Successful replacement of thermodynamic integration by FEP requires the MTP to reproduce the ab initio phase-space distributions of both complex liquid and solid TaVCrW.
SRO provides a stabilization energy of approximately 2-3 meV/atom in TaVCrW.
Electronic-gap effects at the Fermi level modify the TaVCrW phase-space distribution and can shift its melting point by tens of kelvin.
The initial TaVCrW state is a random solid solution at 0 K.
The baseline DFT setup neglects electronic excitations and magnetic fluctuations.
A supercell containing more than 1000 atoms is sufficient to capture significant or percolating SRO clusters.
Large or percolating SRO clusters produce stronger property changes than small ordered clusters.
A supercell that is too small will suppress SRO and consequently produce an inaccurate TaVCrW melting point.
SRO modifies the high-frequency vibrational density of states in the 6-8 THz range.
An accurate MTP enables efficient sampling of the complex liquid and solid phase spaces needed for FEP.
SRO-induced energy barriers in TaVCrW are analogous to diffuse antiphase-boundary energy costs encountered by screw dislocations.
Capturing SRO-associated energy barriers and entropy changes allows FEP to converge rapidly without a thermodynamic-integration path.
SRO stabilizes the solid phase and thereby shifts the TaVCrW melting point.
At 2000 K, the SRO strengthening effect on screw dislocations in MoNbTaW becomes negligible.
The attenuation of SRO-related dislocation strengthening at 2000 K establishes that 2000-2400 K is an appropriate range for validating SRO contributions to TaVCrW melting.
The empirical GGA-PBE/LDA underbinding and overbinding rules fail for V and Cr at 0 K and may propagate errors into the melting calculation.
An MTP that captures SRO can avoid GGA-PBE/LDA bonding errors for V and Cr.
The MTP+FEP melting temperature will be within 10 K of the TOR-TILD baseline.
